module purpose: neorv32_cpu_counters decodes CSR accesses from ctrl_i, controls cycle/instret and hardware-performance counters, stores HPM event-selection masks, and returns selected counter or configuration data on rdata_o. The helper entity neorv32_cpu_counters_cnt implements the writable and incrementing low/high counter words used by the generated counter instances.

use-case flows.value: CSR address and read/write qualification for counter-value and HPM-event accesses
selected counter low or high word written from CSR write data
selected HPM event mask written from ctrl_i.csr_wdata(11 downto 0), with the time-event bit forced to 0
per-counter increment decisions derived from event, debug, halt and HPM-event settings, and counter values incremented when not overwritten
selected counter word or HPM event configuration returned on rdata_o
counter enables, HPM event masks and counter state cleared to zero while rstn_i='0'

conceptual assets.concept: CSR access qualification for counter values and HPM event configuration
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure and read-out flows depend on the module's CSR decode and qualification decisions. Low CSR bits select an entry at line 82, high CSR bits qualify the counter page at lines 90-93 and the HPM-event page at line 94, and the final per-entry read/write decisions are formed in cnt_we, cnt_re, cfg_we and cfg_re at lines 83-86. If these decisions are wrong, a CSR access reaches or returns the wrong stored object. Availability is also established because these decisions are produced whenever the addressed access conditions hold under the relevant generics.

The operate flow stores one increment decision per counter each cycle: cnt_en(0) at line 108, cnt_en(2) at line 110, and cnt_en(3..15) at line 112. Those stored decisions are then delivered to the counter instances as inc_i at lines 131, 150 and 185, and the sub-counter next-state logic uses inc_i at lines 311-312. Integrity is established because a wrong decision changes which counters advance; availability is established under the RTL-visible conditions that the relevant event is present and debug or halt suppression is not active.

Each generated counter instance holds the current count in stored low/high words. A CSR write can load the low or high word from wdata_i when we_i and sel_i select it (lines 302-303 and 325-326); otherwise the counter updates from its increment path, with lo_q taking nxt and hi_q accumulating cy_q (lines 305, 324, 328). Read-back returns the selected word on the sub-counter output at lines 345-349, and the top-level output combines the enabled counter read channels at line 97. Integrity is established because configure, increment and read-out flows all depend on the exact stored count values; availability is established because the values persist across cycles and are returned when the read qualifiers hold. Base counters exist only in the ZICNTR_EN generate block (lines 120-158), and HPM counters only when ZIHPM_EN and HPM_NUM > 0 (lines 171-230); otherwise the corresponding top-level read channels are tied to zero at lines 163-165, 235 and 237.

When HPM support is generated, hpmevent(i) stores a 12-bit configuration from ctrl_i.csr_wdata at lines 199-200, forces the time-event bit low at line 202, participates in HPM increment qualification at line 112, and is zero-extended into CSR read-back when cfg_re(i) is asserted at lines 223-227 before leaving on rdata_o at line 97. Integrity is established because this configuration directly changes which events increment each HPM counter; availability is established because the setting is held, can be read back, and is reset to zero at lines 196-197. This concept exists only when ZIHPM_EN and HPM_NUM > 0; otherwise lines 236-237 tie the configuration and its read channel to zero.
